lessons: ANSWERED: no allocation band after June 2026; section 38(א1) reads 5,000 in the consolidation of 13-07-2026; secondary sources quoting 15,000 (2026) / 10,000 (2027) reflect the superseded 2024 schedule. The regime starts on 5 May 2024, not 1 May.

BRIEF CLAIM NOT ENCODED: '26 characters, prefix A30, rightmost-9 short form' for the allocation number. The Tax Authority FAQ says 9 digits, random, no check digit. Only vendor documentation describes a longer string, so the skill keeps any longer string verbatim and routes to review.

RESOLVED CARRY (4 cycles): the 'pending scripts' note is gone; the skill ships no scripts and says so. If a script is ever written, the Expert's candidate is a deterministic validator (Luhn for ID-number osek numbers, date-aware rate and band, deduction_deadline with month-end clamp, de-dup key, totals).
RESOLVED NEW DEBT (2 cycles): claimant block (status, own number, business type, exempt supplies, filed-through date), vehicle class and document kind, business-use basis, 0-1 fraction.

METHOD LESSON: a single-receipt review missed what a batch user asks. Running the coverage audit on a shoebox query surfaced retention/destruction, de-dup, credit notes and the claimant's status, none of which a per-receipt review reaches.

cycles.trigger: Scheduled staleness pass; brief asked specifically to verify the allocation-number rule and to treat any future threshold row as unsourced.
lessons: ANSWERED (brief question 1): the allocation rule gates the BUYER's input-VAT deduction and does NOT invalidate the invoice. Section 38(א1) sits in the input-tax chapter; section 47(א2)(3)(ג)(2) expressly permits issuing an invoice with no allocated number; invalidity is section 50. This skill already had it right. A sibling skill in the catalogue reportedly says 'the invoice is invalid' and is wrong.

ANSWERED (brief question 2): there is NO 2027 allocation band. NIS 5,000 is the figure in the primary statute (section 38(א1)), not a transitional step, so the phase-in is complete. Verified by string-searching the full consolidated VAT Law: 25,000 and 10,000 appear zero times anywhere in it. Any '2027' row elsewhere in the catalogue is fabricated.

METHOD LESSON: an audit finding proposed adding the regulation 18(ג) full-deduction election. The regulations text reads '(ג) (בוטלה)' -- repealed. Reading the primary source is what stopped a repealed provision being shipped as live law.

NEW DEBT: the 'ITA small-sum threshold' the buyer-identity carve-out hangs on still has no number. The amount lives in the Director's bookkeeping directives, not in the law or the regulations (the phrase 'סכום קטן' appears zero times in both). The skill's habit of naming it without a figure is correct; do NOT let a future cycle fill it in with a guess.

NEW DEBT: document-type codes remain unstated, deliberately. Two live numbering systems disagree (SHAAM has 340 = קבלה and 400 = תעודת חיוב; Green Invoice has 400 = קבלה), so a bare code would be misread. Naming documents rather than coding them stays the right call.
CARRY (3rd cycle): the scripts referenced in earlier cycles are still unshipped. Either write them or drop the references.

METHOD LESSON: the Expert found that regulation 16's hosting bar lived only in a worked example and never in the decision path. An OCR skill that emits a boolean is judged by its AND-list, not by its prose: a rule that is not in the list does not exist. Check every hard-false trigger against the list, not against the document.

NEW DEBT: the JSON record still has no field for the claiming business's own osek number, the vehicle class, whether a vehicle document is a purchase or a running cost, or the business-use share. The decision path now reads state the record cannot hold. Add them next cycle.
Deferred: ship the actual scripts/receipt_parser.py + export_csv.py + references files, or keep the 'pending' note; next cycle decide.
If a checksum for the osek/H.P. number is ever added it must be Luhn mod-10, not invented.

Expert review caught a silent over-claim: deductibility was set true from the SUPPLIER side alone. Israeli input VAT requires the invoice be issued in the BUYER's name (matched to the business's osek), plus date-aware allocation threshold, vehicle/fuel + mixed-use restriction (2/3 or 1/4, not full), the 6-month claim window, and a foreign tax-line guard. Added buyer_name/buyer_vat_number and made vat_deductible conjunctive across all gates.

Deferred: programmatic buyer-osek matching needs the business's own osek as config/user input; the skill instructs to obtain it but ships no config mechanism (tied to the unshipped scripts/). Decide alongside the scripts next cycle.

STALE fixed: the allocation-number '(current)' label sat on the 10,000 band; current is 5,000 since 1 Jun 2026. Moved '(current)' to the 5,000 band in both languages (HE was inconsistently labelled '(previous)' on 10k with no current marker). Date-aware validation logic was already correct.

Check-digit re-confirmed: calling the 9-digit osek/ID check 'Luhn mod-10' is CORRECT (for a 9-digit odd-length number the Israeli 1,2,1,2 weighting is palindromic and identical to Luhn); the earlier suspicion it was wrong was itself wrong.

MAJOR added: cash-law NIS 6,000 business cash-cap warning (the scanner captures payment.method + total, uniquely positioned to warn); Eilat/zero-rated branch so a legitimately VAT-less Israeli receipt is not flagged as an error or auto-classified osek-patur.

Judge caught a pre-existing factual error: 'Receipts (type 320) do not require allocation numbers' - ITA code 320 = חשבונית מס/קבלה, which DOES require one above threshold (plain receipt=400, proforma=332). Restated by document NAME to avoid the wrong code and the self-contradiction.

CRITICAL x2 (expert, pre-existing): (1) no business-purpose gate - vat_deductible could be true for a private-consumption invoice in the business's osek number; added a 'for the business, not private consumption' gate + force needs_review/false for private categories. (2) missing small-sum carve-out - a valid small חשבונית מס / קופה-רושמת slip below the ITA small-sum threshold may omit the buyer VAT number and IS deductible; stop hard-denying no-buyer small slips (needs_review, defer to bookkeeper); a LARGE no-buyer invoice stays false.

MAJOR (expert): commercial/work vehicles (רכב מסחרי, truck, taxi) get FULL input-VAT deduction, not the passenger-car 2/3 restriction; imported GOODS deduct via the customs import entry (רשימון יבוא), not a services self-invoice. Minors: named the self-invoice (חשבונית עצמית); credit-card voucher not a tax invoice; removed 'reduced VAT rate' wording (Israel has none); hedged reverse-charge for a non-full-deducting osek.
Judge caveat: the cash-law gov.il URL (departments/general/reducing_cash_use) 404s; repointed evidence to the Bank of Israel cash-reducing-law page.
